text: San Carlos is a town and municipality located in the Colombian department of Antioquia, within the Eastern Antioquia subregion. It is known as the hydro-electrical capital of Colombia due to its numerous dams and significant energy production. According to the 2018 census, the population of San Carlos was 14,480. The town's site was discovered by Captain Francisco Nuñez Pedroso and was officially founded on 14 August 1786. The municipal area covers 702 km² and includes three corregimientos: El Jordán, Puerto Garzas, and Samaná del Norte. San Carlos is situated three hours from Medellín, the departmental capital, connected by a road. Its geographic coordinates are 6°11′23″N 74°59′49″W (6.18972°N 74.9969°W).
